summary: The registration policy for the NETCONF Capability URNs registry, set by RFC 6241, was stricter than needed. This best current practice changes it to IETF Review, which also allows registrations from certain well-reviewed Experimental RFCs. It updates RFC 6241.

plainLanguage.summary: RFC 7803 changes the review rule for entries in the NETCONF Capability URNs registry. Carefully reviewed non-Standards-Track RFCs can now request entries under the IETF Review policy.

questions: what policy governs netconf capability urn registrations
subtitle: A Best Current Practice changes how NETCONF capability URNs are reviewed.

tldr.problem: The NETCONF Capability URNs registry allowed registrations only from Standards Track RFCs, which the RFC says was unnecessarily strict.
tldr.mechanism: RFC 7803 changes the registry policy to IETF Review. Non-Standards-Track RFCs need IETF Last Call, consultation with relevant working groups, and confirmation of appropriate review during IESG evaluation.
tldr.outcome: The change broadens which reviewed RFCs may register capability URNs and updates RFC 6241.

today: RFC 7803 is a Best Current Practice that updates RFC 6241. It changes the NETCONF Capability URNs registry policy to IETF Review.

sections.title: Why the Registration Rule Changed
sections.content: RFC 6241 set the NETCONF Capability URNs registry to Standards Action, allowing registrations only from Standards Track RFCs. RFC 7803 says this policy proved unnecessarily strict because certain Experimental RFCs and registry corrections in Informational RFCs may also need entries.
sections.plainLanguage: The old rule limited registry entries to Standards Track RFCs. The IETF decided that this excluded some work that had received careful review.

sections.title: The IETF Review Process
sections.content: RFC 7803 changes the registration policy to IETF Review and adds the document as a registry reference. A registration from an RFC outside the Standards Track needs careful review through IETF Last Call and consultation with relevant working groups. The Operations and Management Area Directors should confirm the review during IESG evaluation.
sections.plainLanguage: More kinds of RFCs can seek a registry entry, but they must go through IETF review. The relevant area directors check that the review was appropriate.

sections.title: Scope and Security
sections.content: This document changes a registry procedure and updates RFC 6241. IANA changed the NETCONF Capability URNs registry policy to IETF Review. RFC 7803 describes itself as procedural and says it has no related security considerations.
sections.plainLanguage: The change concerns how registrations are reviewed. It does not add a protocol feature, and the RFC says it has no related security considerations.
